why: The student does not trace the code or say what it prints. Instead they delete the v >= 0 filter on the everyday assumption that rain values are always fine, even though the given input contains -2, so negative values would be added to sum and count and the average would be wrong.

concepts.why: The student says nothing about how v >= 0 is evaluated.
The if is only mentioned as something deleted; no rule about the if statement is stated or applied.
The empty statement is not discussed.
The while loop is not discussed.

concepts.quote: I removed if (v >= 0) because rain values are always fine.
concepts.why: The student uses an everyday idea about rain data instead of the code's filtering rule. Without the filter, -2 would be added (sum 8, count 3, about 2.67 instead of 5.0); this is the NegativeNotFiltered error.
